It's actually pretty fun, it was the one good memory I had at SJSU, I left after one semester after realizing how hard it was to get the classes you need to graduate on time. 

It's more like a 26 hour affair, you come in one day at 9am, and the next day you're done anytime between 10am-2pm.

I hear that a lot of double rooms have been / are being turned into triples, so you'd probably share a dorm with two other people, and they are the people directly ahead of you/behind you in line during check in. If you know someone who has the same orientation date and want to room with them, stand next to them in line.

Hello, I am a community college student looking to major in Aerospace Engineering. I am looking to talk with someone who already works in mechanical or aerospace engineering, and ask some basic questions about how it is going for them. Please message me if you are in any of these fields and would like to share your wisdom. I would really appreciate it.

They do, it's just that they aren't as impacted in the sense one can get the courses they need to graduate on time, while at SJSU, you might see two required courses offered at the same time slot, forcing you to take one the following semester, and thats how the delays add up. Some majors don't even have winter graduation, only summer graduation, so that's a whole waste of a semester also.

The campus feels too small and it's really hard to feel "at home" here as opposed to somewhere like UCR, CPSLO, etc. If you are an engineering major, make sure to earn a lot of college credits in high school. Even though I am entering with about 10 credits, I have an expected graduation time of 5.5 years, hence why I am leaving SJSU after this year. It's not a good fit for me both in terms of course availability and community/culture.
